title: IonQ lands up to $300M DARPA quantum validation deal
source_used: IonQ press release (ionq.com); Fierce Network copy returned HTTP 403
key_facts: IonQ said on 7 Oct 2026 that it advanced to Stage C of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI).
IonQ and DARPA signed a Stage C agreement with a potential value of up to $300 million.
Funding beyond the initial obligation remains subject to future appropriations and DARPA funding actions.
Stage C runs through 2029 and puts multiple generations of IonQ's Superion systems through DARPA's independent verification and validation.
IonQ says it is among the first companies to reach this stage; its sixth-generation machine is Superion 256.
Yesterday's pool item (X12, Quantum Computing Report) reported IBM and three other makers reaching the final round.
quote_evidence: IonQ and DARPA have signed a Stage C agreement with a potential value of up to $300 million to continue validating IonQ's approach to delivering large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers.
Funding beyond the initial obligation remains subject to future appropriations and DARPA funding actions.
why_it_matters_hint: DARPA will test IonQ's machines for years under an agreement worth up to $300 million.
notes: Company press release dated 7 Oct 2026 (before the 8 Oct cutoff), so scored down one. Follow-up of the 8 Oct item on the DARPA final-round selections. Fierce Network carries the release and was blocked.
